name: Aaron Jayjack
location: Saskatchewan/Manitoba, Canada (home base); USA (storm chasing across Great Plains)
story_summary: Aaron Jayjack is an extreme storm chaser and severe weather videographer who has been documenting tornadoes with Insta360 cameras since at least 2024. In June 2025 Insta360 sent him a new X5 kit for peak Canadian Prairie storm season. On June 16, 2025 he stationed himself west of the Wallace/Wallfleet tornado in rural Nebraska — one of the most photogenic tornadoes he has ever seen — and let the camera run for 77 minutes while the slow-moving twister completed its full lifecycle under backlit sunlight. He condensed the footage into a 1-minute '360 reframe timelapse' published on his YouTube channel Jayjack Storm Trax, on Facebook, and on Twitter. PetaPixel covered the footage on June 25, 2025; AccuWeather, TwistedSifter, and InspireMore independently covered it. He describes his mission as helping people experience what he experiences during a tornado intercept.
why_it_matters: A 25-year veteran storm chaser has pioneered an Insta360-specific creative format — the '360 reframe timelapse' — that compresses hours of tornado fieldwork into 1-minute cinematic loops. His Wallace/Wallfleet timelapse attracted coverage from PetaPixel, AccuWeather, TwistedSifter, and InspireMore. The '360 reframe timelapse' technique is entirely specific to 360 cameras — it cannot be replicated with a conventional action camera — making this a compelling Insta360 format story.

name: Edgar O'Neal
story_summary: Edgar O'Neal is a professional storm chaser, weather journalist, and public safety educator based in central Oklahoma. In May 2013 he and his wife had to flee the El Reno tornado — the widest tornado ever recorded (2.6 miles wide) — in a car. The experience transformed him from a musician into a full-time storm chaser dedicated to helping the public understand severe weather. He has been chasing for over ten years and has seen hundreds of tornadoes. Since at least April 2025 O'Neal uses an Insta360 camera for POV storm-chasing content shared with his 476K TikTok followers and 155K Instagram followers. His own TikTok captions include: 'Man thiss Insta360 camera is so much fun!' and 'POV: A #storm is chasing you! @insta360_official #insta360.' He also served as camera operator for Reed Timmer's Dominator 3 team during at least one April 2025 tornado intercept where Insta360 footage was shared by Timmer captioning it '@insta360_official video of a #tornado yesterday! @Edgar ONeal - Storm Chaser was behind the camera!'
why_it_matters: An El Reno tornado survivor who became a storm chaser uses Insta360 cameras to bring 360-degree POV storm education to 476K TikTok followers. His content is explicitly designed to help the public understand severe weather and stay safe. His transformation from music to storm-chasing public educator, triggered by the widest tornado in recorded history, gives him one of the most compelling personal origin stories in the potential Insta360 creator universe.
